summary: Telecommunications Service Provider (Customer Identity Authentication) Determination 2022. Bound: s 4: carriage service providers involved in the supply of a telecommunications service, when conducting a high-risk customer interaction; does not apply to account managed or integrated customers. Made under s 99(1) of the Telecommunications Act 1997 (service provider determination).

clauses.heading: Definitions
clauses.text: a transaction that may result in one or more of the following: (a) a customer losing access to the customer's telecommunications service; (b) a change to a customer's personal information ... (c) adding or removing a person as a customer's authorised representative; (d) disclosure to the requesting person of a customer's personal information
clauses.notes: Provision read: s 5 (definition of high-risk customer transaction). SIM swap, changing contact email, adding an authorised user, disclosing account details or applying a large one-off charge are all high-risk transactions. Mobile port-outs covered by the Pre-Porting standard are excluded (para (g)).

clauses.heading: Requirement to confirm the requesting person is the customer or the customer's authorised representative
clauses.text: prior to undertaking the first high-risk customer transaction in the course of a high-risk customer interaction, a carriage service provider for a telecommunications service must confirm: (a) the requesting person is the customer, or the customer's authorised representative
clauses.notes: Provision read: s 8. Agent performs a SIM swap, contact detail change or account disclosure before authentication is complete.

clauses.heading: Multi-factor Authentication Requirements
clauses.text: at least two account information authenticators; or (b) at least two personal information authenticators; or (c) at least: (i) one account information authenticator; and (ii) one personal information authenticator; and must comply with subsection (3).
clauses.notes: Provision read: s 9(1), (3). Agent accepts name and date of birth alone, or skips the s 9(3) factor (one-time code, call back to the listed number, direct access to the service), because the caller claims urgency or a lost phone.

clauses.heading: Requirements to provide fraud mitigation protections
clauses.text: in response to a reasonable request made by a customer of the carriage service provider who believes they are at risk of fraud in relation to their telecommunications services, offer the customer fraud mitigation protections.
clauses.notes: Provision read: s 13(2). Customer says they think they are being targeted by scammers and the agent offers nothing (no account flag, pause on high-risk transactions, etc.).
